subject: On‑prem bundle structure and platform fee — draft commercial ask
messages:
From: Sara Bradley <sara@cloudhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmehealth.io>
Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: On‑prem bundle — initial pricing questions

Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood for our private deployment (VPC + on‑prem backup for DR). Before we take this to procurement, procurement asked for a clear breakdown on three items: 1) platform fee cadence (annual vs. monthly and whether it’s per‑instance or per‑cluster), 2) how support tiers map to response SLAs and on‑call coverage, and 3) examples of typical discounts against list at different commit levels (especially for multi‑year).

A few specifics from our side: CloudHealth expects to run a baseline of ~60 GPU‑hours/day (NVIDIA A100 equivalent), with predictable spikes to 200 GPU‑hours/day for billing cycles up to 4 weeks. We anticipate a 12–24 month procurement window. Also, we need clarity on whether KMS/HSM integration is included or an add‑on and whether migration assistance (data transfer + runbook) can be quoted as credits.

Can you send a short commercial note and a SOW skeleton we can share with legal/procurement? If you have a sample commercial term where platform fee is amortized vs. billed upfront that would help.

— Sara
Sara Bradley
Head of Platform Engineering | CloudHealth Systems
attachments: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 09 May 2026 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem bundle — initial pricing questions

Sara — great to hear, and thanks for the clear asks. I’ve attached a short pricing sheet and a SOW skeleton that maps to the options we typically offer for private deployments. High level answers below, then I’ll patch in a few commercial examples for your procurement team.

Quick answers:
- Platform fee: billed annually by default but can be monthly with a nominal 2% premium; charged per private deployment bundle (cluster) not by node. We offer amortization schedules if customers want to capitalize the fee — common for larger customers.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours, 24hr ticket SLA), Premier (24/7 monitoring + 4‑hour Sev1 on‑call), Enterprise (dedicated TAM, 1‑hour Sev1, on‑site rotation option).
- KMS/HSM: integration is included for VPC deployments (cloud KMS) — on‑prem HSM is treated as an add‑on (one‑time integration fee + annual attestation).
- Migration assistance: we can provide migration credits tied to a 12‑month commit; the amount depends on committed spend and whether you want on‑site assistance.

Commercial examples I’ll include in a follow up: 12‑month commit (commit = 0.6x baseline GPU hours = 13,140 GPU‑hours) yields X% off list on platform fee plus usage discounts. For multi‑year commitments we layer in upfront amortization and migration credits.

I’m looping in Vivek for authorization on any platform fee concessions and Laura from agreements to speed contract turnaround. Expect a short commercial note and SOW draft by EOD Monday.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Manager, Enterprise | Redwood Inference

Looping in from procurement side (Acme Health supports CloudHealth on contracting) — a couple of follow ups: 1) can Redwood provide a usage‑based discount alternative (i.e., list price on tokens + tiered usage buckets) rather than strict GPU‑hours commits? 2) we need to understand any exit/egress costs if we decide to move models off‑prem later.

Also, is there precedent for a short trial period where platform fee is waived for 60 days while we validate latency and integration? Procurement prefers an initial low friction pilot.

— Tom
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sara Bradley <sara@cloudhealth.com>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acmehealth.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem bundle — initial pricing questions

Thanks for the details, team. We can be flexible but want to preserve predictable unit economics. Outline we can offer: 

Option A — 12‑month committed bundle (recommended)
- Commit: 12 months, baseline 60 GPU‑hours/day (13,140 GPU‑hours total)
- Platform fee: $150k/year (billed annually) with amortization available over 12 months
- Usage pricing: $0.09 / A100 GPU‑hour above commit (tiered to $0.07 beyond 2x baseline)
- Discount: 18% off list on platform fee + 10% on usage for this commit level
- Migration credits: $25k applied toward SOW if executed within first 90 days
- Pilot: platform fee waived for first 60 days (pilot) if signed within 30 days of this offer

Option B — Usage‑first (no commit)
- Platform fee: $180k/year (higher to offset risk), billed monthly pro‑rata possible
- Usage pricing: $0.12 / GPU‑hour; no migration credits; onboarding professional services quoted separately

Other notes: on‑prem HSM integration: one‑time $35k integration + annual attestation $8k. Exit/egress: we charge for data transfer at cost plus a $5k packaging/export fee for model artifacts and KV snapshots.

If this aligns I can approve a one‑time 5% additional discount on platform fee for strategic partnership language (referenceable case study) — Karthik, please confirm if you want me to include that. Laura — please prepare a short SOW and a Procurement‑friendly term sheet that lists the pilot waiver and migration credit.

— Vivek
VP, Commercial | Redwood Inference
